Using the application¶

Virtual environment¶

From the project root:

  1. Create a virtual environment with python -m venv venv.

  2. Activate it (source venv/bin/activate on macOS/Linux, or venv\\Scripts\\activate on Windows).

  3. Install packages with pip install -r requirements.txt.

  4. Copy .env.example to .env and set your own MariaDB password and DJANGO_SECRET_KEY. Never commit .env.

  5. Create the MariaDB database and user described in README.md.

  6. Run python manage.py migrate and python manage.py runserver.

Docker¶

Docker Compose starts MariaDB and the Django app together. From the project root:

docker compose up --build

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ . The Compose file reads passwords from your .env file when that file exists. If it does not, it uses the local development placeholders shown in docker-compose.yml. Replace those placeholders before using the stack anywhere other than your own machine.

Stop the stack with docker compose down.

Rebuild the documentation¶

The HTML in docs/_build/html is already generated. To rebuild it after you change docstrings, install Sphinx and run:

pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
sphinx-build -b html docs docs/_build/html
